I will keep my land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to get grain from the same fields and I already know how to manage it well. Since I am 68 and some family members work off-farm, I will not choose a plan that needs too much hand labor. I have well irrigation, so I will use it to protect wheat and maize at the key stages, but I still want to keep costs under control. I will leave a smaller part of the land for cotton because I have long experience with it and it helps me spread risk, but I will not make cotton too large because it takes more attention. For wheat I will use improved seed, steady fertilizer, and a few irrigations for stable yield. For maize I will use hybrid seed, enough nitrogen, and simpler field management after wheat harvest. For cotton I will also keep inputs moderate, with fewer irrigations than grain crops but more pesticide sprays because insects are a bigger problem there. I will mainly use rotary tillage because it is easier and fits my labor situation.
